plugins.name: brand-capture
plugins.tagline: One-time brand setup. Scans a site and writes the brand files every other skill reads.
plugins.what: Builds BRAND.md once, when a client is set up, so no skill has to ask about the brand again. It scans the public website (about and story pages, products and prices, colors, fonts, blog style, social links, disclaimers) and reads any brand book you give it. It asks four short questions a website can't answer, then writes the brand files.
steps: It asks whether the brand has an existing store or website and a brand book, and which theme is your staging theme (it offers to create one named "<live theme> staging" if you have none). The brand files are saved in its folder.
It scans the website and reads the brand book if you provided one.
It asks four questions in one message: top 3 competitors, inspiration brands, who approves things, and anything the brand must never say or claim.
It studies each inspiration brand and records in BRAND.md what the brand can learn from it.
It writes the files and asks at most four follow-up questions for anything the scan could not settle.
produces: BRAND.md (brand identity, the source of truth)
BRAND-VOICE.md (how the brand sounds)

design.md (a complete visual guide: palette, the full H1 to H6 type scale, spacing, corners, components, imagery and a value for every Shopify theme setting; gaps the sources leave are filled with clearly labelled proposed values)
BRAND.html (a readable copy for the client)
BRAND-QUESTIONS.md (open follow-up questions)
requires: Nothing. Start here.
guardrails: Scans public pages only.
Optional shared copy of the non-confidential files for the team.

plugins.name: competitor-research
plugins.tagline: Dated research on the top 3 competitors named in BRAND.md.
plugins.what: Turns the client's top 3 competitors into COMPETITORS.md. Inspiration brands are not covered here; brand-capture asks for and studies them. For each competitor it compares where they operate against the client, what they sell and at what price, pricing model (flat, packages, memberships, subscriptions), offers and referral programs, how often they publish and who writes it, and how they position themselves. It ends with concrete openings for the client.
steps: It takes the top 3 competitors from BRAND.md. If none are listed, it asks you for your top 3.
It researches each competitor and compares it with the client.
It writes COMPETITORS.md next to BRAND.md and lists openings for the client.
produces: COMPETITORS.md (dated, re-run every few months)
requires: brand-capture (BRAND.md)
guardrails: Never changes BRAND.md.

plugins.name: styles-builder
plugins.tagline: Turn a brand book or reference store into design tokens and apply them to the theme.
plugins.what: Creates or deepens design.md (typography, color schemes, spacing, corner radius, shadows, buttons, component states) and applies those tokens into the theme's settings_schema.json and settings_data.json. It also sets up what a new theme needs before pages get built: logo and favicon, motion, input fields, and variant pickers and swatches. Optionally it brands the starter section templates. When a brand font is not free in Shopify's font library and its files are not already in your working folder, it asks you once for the font files (woff2 preferred, with the licence), instead of guessing or swapping in a lookalike. It never overwrites a brand look that already exists and runs once: on a fresh theme it applies the whole look (settings, custom CSS, fonts); on a theme that already has a look it only finds the holes (low contrast, inconsistent fonts, colours or spacing, weak line spacing) and fixes those, and once it has finished it does not run again until you ask.
prompts: Set up the brand's colors and fonts in the theme
Get the theme ready to build on
steps: If BRAND.md or design.md are missing, it runs brand-capture first and waits for it to finish.
It reads your theme and decides: fresh (still the theme's own look), established (a brand look is already there) or already done. If it already ran, it stops and says so.
Fresh theme: it builds the full token set from your brand book or a reference store, and fills any gap with a labelled proposed value so every theme setting gets one.
It checks each font. If a font is not free in Shopify's library and its files are not in your folder, it asks you for the files once, before changing the theme.

Fresh theme: it applies the tokens into the theme settings and the brand stylesheet and sets up the starter essentials. Established theme: it measures the gaps instead, shows a table (where, now, proposed, why) and changes only the rows you approve, leaving everything else and your own custom CSS as they are.
It records that it ran, so it does not run again unless you ask (a rebrand or new brand book counts as asking).
If you opted in at the start, it brands the starter section templates.
produces: design.md
Updated settings_schema.json and settings_data.json
Logo, favicon, motion, input and variant picker setup (fresh theme)
A gap table with before and after for each fix (established theme)
requires: brand-capture
guardrails: Never overwrites an existing brand look: on an established theme it changes only the gaps you approve.
Runs once. After it finishes, it only runs again when you say so.
Starter section styling only happens if you opt in when it starts.
Never swaps a lookalike font silently, and never downloads or uploads a font file without your yes naming the file, source, size and licence.

plugins.name: blog-generator
plugins.tagline: Research and write SEO and AEO blog posts, delivered as hidden Shopify drafts.
plugins.what: Writes blog posts meant to be found in Google and cited by AI answer engines. It asks intent, media, delivery, mode and topic once, reads BRAND.md and COMPETITORS.md instead of re-asking about the brand, researches what changes each time, and shows the outline for approval before writing.
prompts: Write a post for my store
Write a buying guide for X
Make a how-to article about X
I need a blog post for better SEO
steps: It checks what it needs first (web search, your brand files, Shopify connected for a hidden draft) and walks you through setting up anything missing, in plain steps.
Answer the setup questions once: intent, media, delivery, mode, topic.
It researches the topic and shows the outline in chat.
You approve the outline.
It delivers a hidden Shopify draft, or paste-ready HTML, with SEO fields, images, schema and internal links.
produces: A hidden Shopify draft (via connector or browser), or paste-ready HTML
SEO fields, images, schema, internal links
requires: brand-capture (BRAND.md). competitor-research is optional but used when present.
Web search in Claude. Recommended: Shopify connected (connector or a signed-in browser) for a hidden draft instead of HTML, Python 3 for the QA check, and fact-check installed.
No need to set these up in advance: it checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: Posts land as hidden drafts for a human to review.
Guided mode or fully automated mode. Also runs from blog-autopilot.

plugins.name: blog-rewriter
plugins.tagline: Rewrite an existing article in the store's brand voice and post it as a hidden draft.
plugins.what: Takes a finished article written by someone else (a URL, Google Doc, .docx, .txt or .md file, or pasted text) and rewrites it in the store's voice. It is a voice transplant: facts and claims never change, only wording, tone, rhythm and terminology. Four depths are available: Match, Reword, Restructure and Reimagine.
prompts: Rewrite this doc for the blog
Put this article in our voice
Make this guest post on brand
Clean this up and post it as a draft
steps: It checks what it needs first (web search, your brand files, blog-generator, Shopify connected, and Google Drive or a Word reader for those sources) and walks you through setting up anything missing, in plain steps.
Give it the article and choose a rewrite depth.
It rewrites in the voice from BRAND.md and the live blog, then fact-checks.
It posts a hidden draft with SEO fields and a preview link.
If Shopify is unavailable or not signed in, it returns paste-ready HTML and a fields sheet and says why.
produces: A hidden Shopify draft with SEO fields and a preview link
Fallback: paste-ready HTML and a fields sheet
requires: blog-generator
brand-capture (BRAND.md)
Web search in Claude. Recommended: Shopify connected and Python 3 (required for series and image transfer). Google Drive connected for Google Doc sources.
No need to set these up in advance: it checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: Never quietly changes a claim. Anything changed is flagged.
Posts are hidden drafts only.

plugins.name: blog-autopilot
plugins.tagline: Decides when a store should blog and what to cover, then hands off to the writer.
plugins.what: The editor-in-chief. It scans store events (new products, restocks, rising sellers), Search Console exports, review and helpdesk exports, competitor blog feeds, trends and an occasion calendar, scores the opportunities, and applies guardrails: dedupe, cannibalization, cooldowns and a weekly cap. It never writes the post itself.
prompts: What should we blog about this week?
Set up blogging on a schedule
Is anything worth a new post right now?
steps: It checks what it needs first (a folder, Shopify connected, Python, Search Console and review exports) and walks you through setting up anything missing, in plain steps.
It runs a weekly scan and scores opportunities.
By default it checks in with you and drafts only after you say yes.
It hands the brief to blog-generator, which writes a hidden draft.
Optional: turn on auto-draft.
produces: A ranked list of post opportunities
A brief handed to blog-generator
requires: blog-generator
brand-capture
The Claude desktop app with a folder, Shopify connected, Python 3, and the computer awake with Claude open for the weekly check-in. Recommended: Search Console, review and helpdesk exports.
No need to set these up in advance: it checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: Check-in first, draft only after approval, unless auto-draft is on.
Each brand keeps its own profile.

plugins.name: fact-check
plugins.tagline: Independent fact-check for blog and marketing copy, with guardrails for regulated claims.
plugins.what: Pulls out every factual claim, flags the risky ones (FDA and other regulatory status, medical and treatment claims, ingredient facts, pregnancy and safety statements, clinically proven, statistics), checks them against primary sources, and returns a claim-by-claim report with verdicts, citations and safer rewrites.
prompts: Check the FDA wording in this copy
steps: It checks what it needs first (web search, and your brand files if you have them) and walks you through setting up anything missing, in plain steps.
Give it pasted text, a file, a URL or a Shopify article.
It lists each claim and marks which are risky.
It verifies against authoritative sources.
You get verdicts, citations and safer wording.
produces: A claim-by-claim report with verdicts, citations and safer rewrites
requires: Web search in Claude. Works on its own or after blog-generator. Brand files and Python 3 recommended.
No need to set these up in advance: it checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: It flags and verifies. It never approves.
Regulated claims still need a qualified human or legal review.

plugins.name: seo-audit
plugins.tagline: Check a blog post after it goes live, then track real Search Console rankings.
plugins.what: Audits the live page with Google's own tools: structured data and Rich Results, PageSpeed Insights, title, meta, H1, leftover placeholders and indexing. About two and four weeks later it follows the post's real ranking numbers from Search Console.
prompts: How is the blog post doing in Google?
steps: It checks what it needs first (a browser, Search Console access, an optional free PageSpeed key) and walks you through setting up anything missing, in plain steps.
Run it on publish day to check the live page.
Run it again around week 2 and week 4 for ranking numbers.
It can also run from a scheduled daily blog check.
produces: A live-page audit and ranking follow-ups at 2 and 4 weeks
requires: A browser Claude can use, and Search Console access for the ranking checks. Recommended: Shopify connected and a free PageSpeed API key. Pairs with blog-generator.
No need to set these up in advance: it checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: Read-only. It checks the post and changes nothing.

plugins.name: page-studio
plugins.tagline: Audit a page, suggest what to change or refresh, then change it or build a new one on your staging theme.
plugins.what: Five skills behind one front door. page-audit is read-only: it checks a page against what its type should do, ranks the fixes, and also suggests content and layout refreshes so the page feels current, not only fixed. page-create builds a new page, section or section type. page-edit-content changes words, images and links. page-edit-design changes layout, order, spacing, colour and style, and also offers a layout refresh. page-studio is the front door that picks the right one and chains them. Every visual check is done at both desktop and mobile. It is built for the Site Editor, for marketing and ops people who aren't developers.

skills.name: page-audit
skills.tagline: Read-only gap analysis, ranked, with an owner for every fix and fresh content and layout ideas.
prompts: What should we improve on the homepage?
Where does this page fall short?
How could this page feel fresher?

skills.name: page-create
skills.tagline: Build a new page, a section, or a section type on your staging theme.
prompts: Make a landing page for X
Add a testimonials section to the homepage
Recreate this page from the live site

skills.name: page-edit-content
skills.tagline: Change the words, images and links of an existing page.
prompts: Swap the image on the homepage hero

skills.name: page-edit-design
skills.tagline: Change layout, order, spacing, colour or style of an existing page.
prompts: Make the hero shorter on mobile

skills.name: page-studio
skills.tagline: The front door: picks the right skill and chains them.
prompts: Improve the homepage and apply the top fixes
Check the change I just made
How could the homepage feel fresher?
Make a landing page for X
steps: Each skill first checks what it needs (a browser, your brand files, and a way to reach your theme: the Shopify CLI, or your Shopify connection if it is allowed to change themes) and, if anything is missing, walks you through setting it up in plain steps.
Start with page-audit. Say what the page is for: book, sell, promote, build trust, inform or fix.

It checks the rendered page at both desktop and mobile against a playbook for its type, and names who owns each fix (this theme, store admin, store settings, a third-party app, or an off-site page). If the site-reader plugin is installed, it reads the page with it first, which is faster and uses fewer steps.

It writes a ranked report and a living PAGE-AUDIT.md, with the fixes first and, separately, ideas to make the page feel fresh: new content, a different layout, a redesign of a section. These are suggestions, never applied unless you pick them.
Ask page-edit-content, page-edit-design or page-create to apply the rows you pick, or name any change or new page directly. The front door chains them when a request needs more than one.
produces: A client-ready audit report and PAGE-AUDIT.md (fixes and refresh ideas)
Changes or new pages on your staging theme, each checked at desktop and mobile
requires: brand-capture (BRAND.md, BRAND-VOICE.md, design.md) for new or rewritten words.

To change pages, one of two ways to reach your theme: Node.js and the Shopify CLI signed in to your store with theme access, or, with nothing to install, your Shopify connection when Shopify has approved it to change themes (the check finds out, and falls back to the CLI steps when it isn't). Also a browser Claude can use and a folder on your computer for notes and file backups. On the connection route the change is checked on the private draft right after it is written, and Theme Check can't run. page-audit needs only a browser and the page address.
No need to set these up in advance: each skill checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: page-audit never edits a theme or store.
Changes go only to your staging theme (chosen once, or created for you). The live theme is never edited, and nothing is published unless you ask in your own words, with two confirmations.

plugins.name: theme-audit
plugins.tagline: The full Lighthouse suite, Shopify's Theme Inspector and Theme Check, read out in plain words, with safe fixes on your staging theme.
plugins.what: Scores a page with the full Lighthouse suite from the command line (speed, accessibility, best practices and SEO, on phone and desktop, several runs each, with the HTML reports saved). It also runs Shopify's Theme Inspector, which shows which theme files take the server longest, and Theme Check, Shopify's own checker for theme code. The result is a plain-language readout like the CRO audit's: a headline, a scorecard, and the first things to fix, each with who owns it (this theme, an app, the store's own content or Shopify). It can run read-only on any live page, or fix what the theme owns on your staging theme after your approval and prove nothing visible changed. Accessibility is fixed to 1.00; speed is reported as a middle value with real-visitor data where Google has it, with no 100 target. It never removes apps, changes words or moves layout. Replaces accessibility-audit, which it includes.
prompts: Run Lighthouse on the product page
Accessibility audit on the product page
steps: It checks what it needs (Node.js, the Shopify CLI, Chrome, Lighthouse) and walks you through setting up anything missing.
It says whether this is an audit only (read-only, no staging theme needed) or an audit with fixes (it uses your staging theme, asked once or created; the live theme is never edited).
It runs the full Lighthouse suite three times on phone and desktop, the Theme Inspector on the page, Theme Check on the theme, and reads Google's real-visitor data.
It gives you a short readout: headline, scorecard, the first things to fix with who owns each, quick wins, and what is not the theme's to fix.
If you choose fixes, it applies the safe ones on your staging theme, checks the page looks and works the same, and re-scores.
produces: A plain-language readout in chat and at the top of THEME-AUDIT.md
Lighthouse HTML and JSON reports for every run
Server timing by theme file, and a theme code check summary
Approved fixes on your staging theme (fix mode only)
requires: Node.js, the Shopify CLI signed in to your store with theme access, Google Chrome, Lighthouse (downloads itself), a browser Claude can use, and a folder on your computer for the theme copy.
No need to set these up in advance: it checks them first and walks you through anything missing, step by step.
guardrails: Audit-only mode changes nothing: no theme, store, app or content is edited.
Never edits the live theme: fixes go to your staging theme. Nothing is published unless you ask.
Never removes or turns off apps and never changes store content; it reports their cost and owner.
Roughly 30 to 60 minutes per page template for every check, 15 to 40 for accessibility alone. These are estimates.

plugins.name: analytics
plugins.tagline: Audit tagging, get tracking working, clean up tags and keep it from breaking.
plugins.what: Four skills sharing one ANALYTICS.md per client site. Analytics is only useful if the numbers can be trusted, and most breakages are silent: a duplicated tag, a renamed button, a consent banner that never reports the visitor's choice. Shopify-first, also WordPress and custom sites.

skills.name: analytics-audit
skills.tagline: Tagging audit and full audit across privacy states. Changes nothing.
prompts: Is our analytics set up correctly?

skills.name: analytics-setup
skills.tagline: From the client's issue list to approved, verified fixes.

skills.name: analytics-cleanup
skills.tagline: Quick cleanup of dead tags, or zero-based deep tag cleanup.
prompts: Our site is slow because of tags

skills.name: analytics-guardrails
skills.tagline: Dependency register, change checks and drift watch.
prompts: Check analytics impact before this theme change

steps: Audit first: it inventories what is installed, what it sends and what should change, with evidence.
Setup runs the full path: issue list, tracking plan, audit, prioritised actions for approval, one fix at a time with a rollback ready, then re-test every core event.
Cleanup removes dead weight, then makes every remaining tag earn its place.
Guardrails checks every later site change against a register of what tracking depends on.
produces: ANALYTICS.md (tracking plan, stack inventory, consent setup, dependency register, findings, changelog)
requires: Python 3 for the scripts. The privacy matrix needs Node and Playwright. The cost benchmark needs Node and Chrome. GA4 checks can use Google's Analytics MCP server.
guardrails: Audit changes nothing.
Setup never skips the approval or the test.

plugins.name: cro-audit
plugins.tagline: Find what is costing conversions, say how sure we are, and plan what to fix and test.
plugins.what: A quick first-pass audit or the full research suite CRO agencies run, with no integrations required. It reviews the live page (technical, speed, mobile, heuristics, competitors), reads the store's Shopify Analytics read-only through the Shopify CLI (or numbers you supply), checks the data can be trusted (tracking breaks, orders by channel, bots), then lays out the funnel stage by stage (each stage's rate by device, channel and entry page, against your targets or the store's own average, with a plain verdict), shows each key problem on a screenshot of the real page with numbered boxes, reviews heatmaps and recordings you bring, mines reviews and support text, writes survey questions and user-test scripts and analyses the results. Every finding is labelled by the kind of evidence behind it and how confident we are. It then sorts issues into just do it, instrument, investigate, test or hypothesize, scores them, and plans experiments with a hypothesis, metrics, sample size and duration. It also checks A/B test results, including whether the traffic split was valid.
prompts: Run a CRO audit on the homepage
Run the full CRO research suite
Here are our funnel numbers, where is the leak?
Plan an A/B test for the booking button
How many visitors do we need for this test?
steps: Choose a quick audit (about an hour, needs nothing from you) or the full audit.
It reviews the live page at desktop and phone width and measures speed.

If the Shopify CLI is authorised for the store it reads the analytics itself, read-only; otherwise bring funnel numbers. Also bring heatmaps or recordings, reviews or support text, past test results if you have them.
It prepares the survey questions and user-test script if you want them, and analyses the answers when they come back.
Give it your target rates per stage if you or your agency have them; otherwise it compares the store with itself, or with a published benchmark it names.

It gives you a plain-language summary in chat (where visitors stop, the top five fixes in a table, quick wins, what to test, what it couldn't check) and writes CRO-AUDIT.md: one block per funnel stage with pictures of the page and numbered changes, then every finding, its evidence and the experiment plans.
produces: CRO-AUDIT.md (funnel by stage with verdicts, ranked findings with evidence and confidence, buckets, scores, experiment plans, open questions)
cro-evidence/: screenshots of the page sections behind each problem, on phone or desktop, with numbered boxes
Survey questions and a user-test script, on request
A slide deck or web page of the same report, only when you ask for one
requires: Nothing for a quick audit (Chrome or Chromium on the computer gives it the screenshots). For analytics: the Shopify CLI authorised for the store with read_reports and read_orders (you grant it yourself), or exported numbers. Uses REVIEW-MINING.md, COMPETITORS.md and BRAND.md if they exist.
guardrails: Strictly read-only: never changes store settings, setup, themes, content or apps, even with access that would allow it, and never submits forms or answers the cookie banner.
Screenshots only load and scroll the page in a fresh private browser; they never click, type or submit.
No invented benchmarks or lift predictions: every target names its source and date.
Small samples are flagged as directional.
It prepares surveys and tests but does not run them; you collect that data.

plugins.name: brand-voice
plugins.tagline: Build the brand's voice, then write on-brand copy with it.
plugins.what: Two skills. voice-builder is a short guided wizard (10 to 15 minutes, one multiple-choice question at a time) that comes right after brand-capture and refines BRAND-VOICE.md: one default voice with the channel exceptions under it, built from your own words, the brand's best-performing ads and a pick-the-one test. copywriter then writes specific, on-brand copy for store sections, emails, captions, interface text and campaigns, checked against the voice and the brand's claim limits.

skills.name: voice-builder
skills.tagline: A guided wizard that builds or refines BRAND-VOICE.md.

skills.name: copywriter
skills.tagline: Writes on-brand copy for the site, email, captions, microcopy and campaigns.

steps: Run voice-builder after brand-capture. It asks how much material to use (Minimal, Regular or Maximal) and finds the brand's best-performing ads even when you name none.
It asks what the brand never says and what makes AI copy feel wrong, sets one default voice with channel exceptions, and runs a pick-the-one test: your picks write the rules.
It records who approves brand decisions and who approves copy, then shows three examples in the new voice beside the old so you can finalize or rework.
Ask copywriter for any piece of copy. It researches the customer's own words first, gives every piece one job, and writes three directions where there is a real choice.
produces: BRAND-VOICE.md (default voice, channel exceptions, approvers)
Copy for store sections, emails, captions, interface text and campaigns, in three directions where it matters
requires: brand-capture (BRAND.md and BRAND-VOICE.md). If BRAND-VOICE.md is thin or missing, copywriter offers voice-builder first.
guardrails: Copy never goes beyond the claim limits in BRAND.md, and regulated or numeric claims are flagged for fact-check.
You pick the voice: nothing is finalized without your picks.

plugins.name: shopify-storefront
plugins.tagline: Plan and launch a campaign, build its landing page, and match the theme to the brand guide.
plugins.what: Three skills for a busy founder who wants results without touching theme settings, all working through the Shopify connector in a normal chat (no terminal) or the Shopify CLI, and always on your staging theme. campaign-launcher plans a time-boxed campaign from one sentence or your materials, keeps the whole plan in one artifact, generates the calendar invite, readies the website, drafts email, SMS and ads as stubs, and puts Launch and Stop reminders on your calendar (it never publishes on its own). campaign-page generates a landing page template that sells, in which every part (hero, trust row, countdown, products, FAQ, signup, closing banner) is its own section with ready alternates you swap with one switch in the theme editor or by asking Claude. theme-editor makes the theme's colours (and fonts if asked) match the brand guide, with a contrast check.

skills.name: campaign-launcher
skills.tagline: One-line plan, one plan artifact, calendar invite with add-to-calendar links, website on your staging theme, channel drafts, Launch and Stop reminders.
prompts: Put the sale on the homepage

skills.name: campaign-page
skills.tagline: A campaign landing page template that sells: one section per part, ready alternates switched off, one-switch swaps, phases from coming soon to ended.
prompts: Show me options for the page
A page for the Black Friday sale

skills.name: theme-editor
skills.tagline: Make the theme match the brand guide, with a before and after table and a contrast check.
prompts: Make the site match our brand guide
Change the brand colors on the website
Make the site match our brand guide
steps: Describe the campaign in a sentence and drop in anything you have (a brief, copy, images, a video, links). campaign-launcher shows one plan line: name, type, exact dates with time zone, and channels, plus a calendar invite. You say yes once.

It readies the announcement bar, homepage hero and an optional countdown, and a landing page, on your staging theme, in the brand's voice. The landing page template is generated from your theme's own sections: each part (hero, trust row, products, FAQ, signup, closing banner) is its own section with ready alternates switched off. Swap one with the eye icon in the theme editor, or say "swap the hero to the video hero". The generator checks every section, block and setting against your theme first, and lists any placeholder text still to replace. Email, SMS and ads are drafted as stubs for you to send.

It puts Launch and Stop reminders on your calendar. When you ask, Launch publishes the staging theme after the checks and two confirmations, and Stop puts the site back exactly as it was. Nothing goes live unless you publish it yourself or ask Claude to, with two confirmations.

For brand colours, give theme-editor your brand guide or hex codes. It shows a before and after table, checks every text and background pair for readable contrast, and delivers it on your staging theme.
produces: A one-line campaign plan, the whole plan in one artifact (brief, plan, website, copy, drafts, links, launch steps), and a calendar invite: add-to-calendar links for the campaign, Launch and Stop, plus a .ics file
A preview theme with the campaign on it and a preview link
A landing page template with ready alternates for each section and a swap map (swap in the editor's eye icon or by asking Claude), and a design draft with two or three copy options
A before and after table for brand colours and fonts, with contrast results
requires: The Shopify connector signed in to the store (the store owner connects it once), or the Shopify CLI.
BRAND.md and BRAND-VOICE.md from brand-capture and voice-builder help; without them, copy is not checked against a brand file.
guardrails: Never edits the live theme: all work is on your staging theme. Going live is your decision: publish it yourself, or ask Claude and confirm twice.
For a store whose live theme is connected to GitHub, work goes to the staging theme and the staging branch, and going live is a merge you ask for and confirm twice.
Email, SMS and ads are drafts only; only the website is connected.
Extras (countdown, badges, sale colours) are offered, never added unasked.
The editor swap is proven on a real staging theme only once; until then the hand-over says it is left for you to check.

plugins.name: site-reader
plugins.tagline: Read a page's text and layout at desktop and mobile without opening a browser.
plugins.what: One command that returns a short summary of what a page says and how it is laid out, so other skills can look at a page quickly and with few steps. A plain text read gives the title, headings, copy, links, structured data and, on Shopify, the theme id. A second read, using the Chrome already on the computer in the background, measures sections top to bottom, the first screen, calls to action, popups in the way, fonts and colours, small tap targets, broken images and sideways overflow, at desktop and mobile. Pictures are saved only when you ask.
prompts: What does the homepage look like at desktop and mobile?
Is there a popup on the first screen?
Which theme is this page using?
steps: Give it a page address. It reads the text first, then the layout at desktop (1440x900) and mobile (375x812).
You get a short summary: sections with positions and heights, a line where the first screen ends, calls to action, anything covering the screen, type and colours as measured.
Ask for pictures (a small first-screen image or a shrunk full-page image per device) only when the numbers aren't enough.
For a Shopify preview, it can check that the page reports the theme you meant.
produces: A short text summary (about a thousand tokens) and a saved report.json
Optional small pictures and a wireframe per device
requires: Python 3 and Chrome or Chromium on the computer (nothing to install). Without Chrome it still reads the text and says what it could not see.
guardrails: Read-only: it loads and scrolls, and never clicks, types or submits.
It never types a password: a locked store is reported as blocked.
Anything about how a page looks is read at both desktop and mobile; what it can't read is marked Can't tell.
